elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence throughout the Agreement term.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause requires a USD 2,000,000 aggregate commercial general liability limit.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Subsection (b) requires professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Subsection (c) requires USD 5,000,000 in cyber and privacy liability insurance where HDI processes data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company. That operative trigger encompasses processing Customer Data.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: Subsection (d) requires workers' compensation insurance as required by law.

elements.element: Vendor must provide certificates of insurance to Customer upon request.
elements.evidence: The final sentence requires HDI to provide certificates of insurance to the Company on request.

elements.element: Vendor must maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative USD 2,000,000 E&O requirement exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback limit.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, Vendor must maintain cyber and privacy liability insurance of at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The operative provision requires USD 5,000,000 in cyber and privacy liability coverage when HDI processes Company data, exceeding the USD 2,000,000 fallback limit.

result.reason: The operative clause fully satisfies the preferred position and therefore also the fallback. It leaves the existing provision unchanged and introduces no contradiction. It is not strictly minimal because the cyber trigger covers any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company, which may be broader than the specified Customer Data trigger. Drafting is otherwise clear, though the new Insurance provision is unnumbered within a numbered section.
